artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ and consider the family of quadratic polynomials
$$P_\lambda(z)=\lambda z+z^2,\qquad \lambda\in\overline{\mathbb{D}}.$$
For $\lambda=e^{2\pi i\alpha}$ with $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$, $P_\lambda$ is said to be linearizable at $0$ if there exists a univalent holomorphic map $h$ defined on a neighborhood of $0$, with $h(0)=0$ and $h'(0)=1$, such that $h^{-1}\circ P_\lambda\circ h(z)=\lambda z$. Let $r_\lambda$ denote the conformal radius of the largest such linearization domain (the Siegel disk), with the convention $r_\lambda=0$ when $P_\lambda$ is not linearizable.

It is known that:
(i) there exists a bounded holomorphic function $U:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ such that $|U(\lambda)|=r_\lambda$ for every $\lambda\in\mathbb{D}$;
(ii) the Brjuno set $\mathcal{B}\subset\mathbb{R}$ consists of those irrationals $\alpha$ whose continued fraction convergents $p_n/q_n$ satisfy
$$B(\alpha)=\sum_{n\ge 0}\frac{\log q_{n+1}}{q_n}<\infty,$$
and $B:\mathcal{B}\to\mathbb{R}$ is the Brjuno function;
(iii) for $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$, $P_{e^{2\pi i\alpha}}$ is linearizable iff $\alpha\in\mathcal{B}$.

Question: Does the function
$$\alpha\;\longmapsto\;B(\alpha)+\log\bigl|U(e^{2\pi i\alpha})\bigr|,$$
defined a priori on $\mathcal{B}$, extend to a $\tfrac12$-Hölder continuous function on all of $\mathbb{R}$?
artifact.status_search_result: This is the Marmi–Moussa–Yoccoz conjecture on the 1/2-Hölder regularity of the function Υ(α)=B(α)+log|U(e^{2πiα})|. Buff and Chéritat proved that the function cannot be α-Hölder for any exponent α>1/2 (sharpness). Cheraghi and Chéritat (2015) proved the 1/2-Hölder continuity for the restriction of Υ to rotation numbers of sufficiently high type, but the conjecture in full generality on all of ℝ remains open as of the most recent literature.

status_evidence.title: A Proof of the Marmi–Moussa–Yoccoz Conjecture for Rotation Numbers of High Type
status_evidence.snippet: Marmi, Moussa and Yoccoz conjectured that a certain error function ... is 1/2-Hölder continuous ... proved for the restriction of Υ to a class of high type numbers.
status_evidence.claim: The 1/2-Hölder conjecture is established only for high-type rotation numbers, leaving the full statement open.

status_evidence.title: The Brjuno Functions and Their Regularity Properties
status_evidence.snippet: A regular perturbation of this equation leads to a modification of the singular function which is 1/2-Hölder continuous.
status_evidence.claim: The 1/2-Hölder regularity statement is the conjecture posed by Marmi–Moussa–Yoccoz.
